gloss: nothing ventured, nothing gained; go for it and accept whatever happens; give it a shot

definitions.gloss: nothing ventured, nothing gained; go for it and accept whatever happens; give it a shot
definitions.explanation: A proverb encouraging bold action despite uncertain outcomes — charge forward even if you might fail.

examples.japanese: {当|あ}たって{砕|くだ}けろの{精神|せいしん}で{挑戦|ちょうせん}した。
examples.english: I took the challenge with a nothing-ventured-nothing-gained spirit.

examples.japanese: {結果|けっか}はわからないけど、{当|あ}たって{砕|くだ}けろだ。
examples.english: I don't know the outcome, but I'll go for it.

examples.japanese: {告白|こくはく}するか{迷|まよ}っていたが、{当|あ}たって{砕|くだ}けろと{思|おも}って{声|こえ}をかけた。
examples.english: I was hesitating about confessing my feelings, but I decided to go for it and spoke up.

notes:
A proverb encouraging bold action despite uncertain outcomes. Literally means "hit it and shatter" — implying you should charge forward even if you might break. The imperative form {砕|くだ}けろ gives it a forceful, motivational tone.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {当|あ}たって{砕|くだ}けろの{精神|せいしん}: the spirit of "go for it"
- {当|あ}たって{砕|くだ}けろだ: (I'll) just go for it
- {当|あ}たって{砕|くだ}けろの{気持|きも}ちで: with a "nothing to lose" attitude

USAGE:
Used when facing a daunting situation — job interviews, confessions, business proposals, or any situation where the outcome is uncertain but inaction is worse. It is an encouragement to take action despite fear of failure.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {虎穴|こけつ}に{入|い}らずんば{虎子|こじ}を{得|え}ず: nothing ventured, nothing gained (more literary)
- とりあえずやってみる: just try it for now — more casual, less dramatic
